skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate, edit, upscale, and stitch AI images through the inference.sh CLI using FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and related models.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh CLI image models for text-to-image, editing, upscaling, and visual workflow examples.
skill.author: inference-sh-8

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown formatting or safe documentation links, not executable Ruby backticks. The real issues are the Quick Start command that pipes a remote installer into sh, the related-skill install commands, and the install note that reassures users after showing an unverifiable execution path.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-sh command with manual download instructions that verify the published checksum before execution.

remediation.issue: Related skill commands install additional community skills from a remote source.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the npx install commands or add explicit review steps and links to separate audits for each related skill.

remediation.issue: The skill does not clearly explain external service data flow.
remediation.suggestion: Document that prompts, image URLs, and source images may be sent to inference.sh or model providers before users run examples.

semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends `curl -fsSL https://cli.inference.sh | sh && infsh login` and later reassures readers that the installer verifies checksums. That sequence still executes a remote script before the user can verify the binary independently.

content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable way to create and edit AI images from a coding assistant. This skill maps prompts to inference.sh CLI workflows for text-to-image, editing, upscaling, and model selection.
actual_capabilities: Lists image generation models and app IDs for FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
Shows inference.sh CLI commands for text-to-image generation with specific model app IDs.
Provides examples for image upscaling and stitching using image URL inputs.
Includes a command to browse available image apps by category.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps and image generation workflows.
limitations: Requires users to install and authenticate with the inference.sh CLI.
Sends prompts, image URLs, or source images to external inference.sh or provider services.
Does not provide a local image generation engine or offline model execution.
Does not verify copyright, trademark, or publicity rights for generated images.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate product scenes, social graphics, and visual directions from concise creative prompts.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Explore mockups, backgrounds, and image edits before commissioning final production assets.

use_cases.title: Automate Visual Experiments
use_cases.description: Compare models, prompts, and image workflows from a terminal-based assistant session.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a square product image of a ceramic coffee mug on a neutral studio background. Use an inference.sh image model suited for product photography.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three visual directions for a cinematic mountain landscape. Recommend which inference.sh image apps to try and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Edit and Upscale an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an image editing workflow to improve lighting, remove distractions, and upscale the final result for a website hero image.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Repeatable Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable workflow that generates four concept images, selects the strongest result, upscales it, and prepares a short usage note for the team.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a studio product image for a new coffee mug launch.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a product-focused image model, drafts a polished prompt, and explains how to run the inference.sh workflow.

output_examples.input: A designer has two source image URLs and wants a single horizontal comparison image.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends the stitching workflow, describes the needed image inputs, and summarizes the expected combined image.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to compare FLUX, Gemini, and Seedream for the same visual brief.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines a controlled model comparison with consistent prompt wording, aspect ratio, and review criteria.

best_practices: Review the CLI installation method before running any remote installer command.
Use clear prompts with subject, style, lighting, composition, and output size requirements.
Check provider terms, privacy needs, and rights constraints before using generated images in production.
anti_patterns: Do not paste sensitive images, private URLs, or confidential prompts into external generation services without approval.
Do not treat generated images as cleared for commercial use without a rights review.
Do not install related skills or CLI tools from remote sources without reviewing their trust boundary.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI images, edits, upscaled outputs, stitched images, and model comparison workflows through inference.sh CLI examples.

faq.question: Does it generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It relies on the inference.sh CLI and external image model providers.

faq.question: Which assistants can use the marketplace listing?
faq.answer: The listing is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users who work with terminal-based workflows.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. The Quick Start shows an inference.sh login step after CLI installation.

faq.question: Can it upscale existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes an example using a Topaz upscaler app with an image URL input.

faq.question: Is the install command safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The remote installer should be reviewed and verified before execution, especially because the Quick Start pipes it to a shell.
